what_its_for: Phenobarbital is used to control and prevent seizures (epilepsy). It may also be used for short-term treatment of anxiety or to help with sleep problems. It works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain.
how_to_take: Take phenobarbital exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food, but taking it with food may help if it upsets your stomach. Try to take it at the same time every day to keep a steady level in your body. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablet unless your doctor says it is okay.
dosing: Your dose depends on your age, weight, and the condition being treated. For seizures in adults, a common dose is 60 to 200 mg taken once daily at bedtime, or divided into smaller doses throughout the day. Children's doses are based on body weight and will be determined by your doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you miss several doses or are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist right away, as stopping suddenly can trigger seizures.
storage: Store phenobarbital at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about safe disposal options or use a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking phenobarbital — it can dangerously increase drowsiness and slow your breathing. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Do not stop taking phenobarbital suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause serious withdrawal symptoms or trigger seizures. Tell your doctor about all other medications, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take, as phenobarbital interacts with many drugs including blood thinners, birth control pills, and antidepressants.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of harming yourself or suicide, unusual mood or behavior changes, severe confusion, difficulty breathing or very slow breathing, severe skin rash or blistering, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), unusual bruising or bleeding, or if your seizures get worse or happen more often. Also call your doctor if you feel very dizzy, have trouble walking, or notice signs of allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, or throat.
when_it_works: Phenobarbital begins working relatively quickly in your body, but it may take several days to weeks before your seizures are fully controlled or you feel the full benefit. Do not stop taking it just because you feel better — it must be taken consistently to keep working. Your doctor will monitor your blood levels and adjust your dose as needed.
special_populations: Older adults (65+): You may be more sensitive to the sedating effects and are at higher risk of falls and confusion. Your doctor may start you at a lower dose. Pregnant women: Phenobarbital can harm an unborn baby, but untreated seizures during pregnancy can also be dangerous. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits. Do not stop taking it without medical advice. Breastfeeding mothers: This medication passes into breast milk and may cause drowsiness or feeding problems in your baby. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Doses are carefully calculated by weight. Phenobarbital can sometimes cause the opposite effect in children, making them hyperactive or irritable instead of sleepy. Tell your doctor if you notice unusual behavior changes.
